The test image shows a young soybean seedling with:
- Brownish stem lesion near the soil line/node area
- Grayish-white fuzzy/cottony growth on the stem
- Small dark specks visible on stem tissue
- Plant appears to be at early seedling stage

Top candidates: **Rhizoctonia** (reddish-brown firm lesions at soil line), **Pythium_damping_off** (water-soaked brown soft rot), **Phytophthora** (dark brown stem lesion from taproot up). Let me check reference images.

**Key visual analysis of test image:**
- Very young soybean seedling at soil level
- Clear brownish lesion/discoloration at the stem node/soil line junction
- Green stem above and below the lesion
- Fuzzy appearance is natural soybean trichomes (stem hairs), not fungal mycelium
- Lesion appears firm and dry (not water-soaked)

**Comparison:**
- **Rhizoctonia**: "reddish-brown, sunken, firm and dry lesions on hypocotyls at the soil line" — matches the browning at the node/soil line, firm lesion appearance, seedling stage
- **Pythium**: water-soaked, soft rot, plants easily pulled — test image doesn't show water-soaked tissue
- **Phytophthora**: dark brown lesion extending from taproot up several nodes — Phytophthora reference shows a similar node lesion pattern but typically on more established plants

The brownish-to-reddish firm lesion at the soil line/hypocotyl on this seedling is most consistent with **Rhizoctonia** seedling blight.
